corrections.was: A list of five old probes. An Invariant is a condition that must stay true throughout, whatever else changes. Here movement, jump, a projectile, reset and a collected coin must all still pass after the checkpoint is added, and five of five still hold. A change that breaks one fails. For example, when an agent adds a dash move to your player, the invariant that the old jump test still passes must hold.
corrections.now: A list of five old checks. An Invariant is a condition that must stay true throughout, whatever else changes. Here movement, jump, a projectile, reset and a collected coin must all still pass after the checkpoint is added, and five of five still hold. A change that breaks one fails. For example, when an agent adds a dash move to your player, the invariant that the old jump test still passes must hold.
corrections.why: The five items are checks from two old probes, not five probes: Chapter 5 says input_probe.gd reports four checks (movement, jump, projectile created, reset) and feature_route.gd collects a coin, and the slide calls invariants 'the existing checks that must still pass'.

corrections.was: Each pair sets look-alike terms side by side. Reverse starts from a game that exists, and its claims are tagged observed. Draft starts from an idea, and tags its guesses as assumptions. Both arrows end in a GDD.
corrections.now: Each pair sets look-alike terms side by side. Reverse starts from a game that exists, and most of its claims are tagged observed. Draft starts from an idea, and tags its guesses as assumptions. Both arrows end in a GDD.
corrections.why: A reverse pass tags claims observed, inferred or missing (Chapter 5 provenance table; the recovered GDD had 107 observed, 29 inferred, 30 missing, as the film shows earlier), so saying all its claims are observed teaches a wrong rule.

corrections.was: The checkpoint should respond well becomes, return the player within zero point two metres of the respawn point within two frames, at a fixed sixty frames per second. Measured, zero point zero eight nine eight metres, under the limit.
corrections.now: The checkpoint should respond well becomes, return the player within zero point two metres of the respawn point within two frames, at a fixed sixty frames per second. Measured in a constructed fixture that sets the player below the fall threshold in code, not by play, zero point zero eight nine eight metres, under the limit.
corrections.why: The 0.0898 m value is AC-01 criterion 5, which Chapter 5 labels 'Constructed fixture, labelled: a direct state write that tests the fall branch, not a fall a player makes'; the bare 'Measured' let it pass as an ordinary play run.
